segments.title: HMS Orion's battle honours, 1939-44
segments.body: HMS Orion's honours begin with Atlantic service in 1939 and Calabria in 1940. Her general Mediterranean honour covers 1940, 1943 and 1944. The 1941 list includes Malta convoy duty, Matapan, Greece and Crete, which makes the missing general Mediterranean honour for that year seem curious. Sicily and Salerno follow in 1943. The 1944 honours cover the Aegean, Anzio, Normandy and southern France. The list shows how often the Royal Navy committed this Leander-class cruiser across several theatres.

evidence.note: The transcript lists Orion's Atlantic, Mediterranean, Greek, Italian, Aegean, Normandy and southern-France battle honours.

segments.summary: HMS Orion's honours span Atlantic service in 1939, Mediterranean campaigns from Calabria to Salerno, and 1944 operations in Normandy and southern France.

segments.title: What battle-honour totals hide
segments.body: Orion's official battle-honour record matches HMS Nubian and HMS Jervis and is surpassed only by HMS Warspite. The comparison jokes that a battleship need only fire its guns to earn a battle honour, while a cruiser or destroyer has to do more. Campaign honours for smaller warships can cover several battles. The argument is that comparable actions by a larger ship would count separately, so a simple tally understates the service behind Orion's honours. The closing tribute calls her a war hero and says she was gone too soon.

evidence.note: The transcript compares Orion with Nubian, Jervis and Warspite, then explains the different battle and campaign-honour treatment of battleships, cruisers and destroyers.

segments.summary: Comparisons with HMS Nubian, HMS Jervis and HMS Warspite introduce the argument that battle-honour totals give an uneven picture of warship service.
